### Observed differences

- The starkest difference concerns the segment between A39 and A24. In the earlier window, A21, A22 and A23 each ran in every one of the 200 traces, always together and in varying order, with A39 always preceding them; in the later window each of the three appears in only about 1 in 200 traces. [OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, REL025, REL026, REL031, REL028, REL033, REL037]
- In the later window, three activities that were not observed at all earlier — A14, A15 and A16 (0 of 200 traces before) — each run in about 30, 33 and 37 in 100 traces; they never co-occur, so essentially exactly one of the three executes per trace. [OCC013, OCC014, OCC015, REL001, REL002, REL010]
- A39's outgoing transitions were redirected: earlier they went to A21/A22/A23 (roughly 35/30/35 in 100 of its outgoing transitions), later to A14/A15/A16 (roughly 30/33/37 in 100), and each of A14/A15/A16 leads on only to A24. [DIR030, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012]
- Ordering and distance moved accordingly: earlier the trio always preceded A24, whereas later A14/A15/A16 precede A24 in every trace in which they occur (30–37 in 100 traces) and A24 usually runs without the trio; the gap from A39 to A24 shrank from four to two event positions, and A24's mean relative position moved earlier (about 0.43 to 0.39). The new activities sit at roughly the relative position (about 0.35) the trio held before. [REL027, REL032, REL036, REL006, REL014, REL021, LAG010, POS007, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- The late cycle between A40 and A41 repeats more often in the later window: A40 averages 1.8 occurrences per trace (1.57 before) and recurs in about 48 in 100 traces (37 before); A41 runs in about 69 in 100 traces (59 before) and averages 0.96 occurrences (0.75 before), with more transitions back and forth between the two (co-occurrence 69 vs 59 in 100, interleaving 42 vs 28 in 100). [OCC029, OCC030, REL044, DIR031, DIR032, DIR033, LAG011, LAG014]
- The group around A02, A06, A07 and A08 is executed more often: each of these runs in about 56 in 100 later traces versus about 47 earlier, while A01, A03, A04 and A05 each fall from about 53–54 to about 43–44 in 100; consistently, A02's exits shift toward A06 and A06's toward A07. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, DIR002, DIR006]
- Smaller routing shifts: A33 now splits its exits about evenly between A30 and A34 (about 60/40 before), A35 sends more to A36 (about 61 vs 55 in 100), and A18 sends more to A29 (about 60 vs 46 in 100). [DIR025, DIR026, DIR027, DIR028, DIR014]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A39 and A24 is executed differently: in the earlier window every case ran the three activities A21, A22 and A23 between A39 and A24 (all three, in no fixed order), whereas in the later window A39 is followed by exactly one of A14, A15 or A16 and then A24, so the intermediate segment shrank from three activities to one and the old trio is essentially no longer executed (about 1 in 200 later traces). [OCC013, OCC014, OCC015, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, DIR030, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, LAG010]

This rests on direct, mutually consistent relational evidence rather than volume alone: A39's successor set changed completely, the new activities lead only to A24, the order relations with A39 and A24 flipped from "always together/always before" to "A24 and A39 without the trio", and the measured A39-to-A24 distance and A24's position moved as expected; the participation swings (0 of 200 to 60–74 of 200 traces, and 200 of 200 down to 1 of 200) are far larger than random re-splits of a stable process produce (empirical strength about 0.995 on these items). [DIR030, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, REL006, REL014, REL021, REL027, REL032, REL036, REL028, REL033, REL037, LAG010, POS007, OCC013, OCC014, OCC015, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022]

An important competing explanation remains: the evidence cannot distinguish a modification of one process from a shift in the mix of case variants between the windows, nor can it show whether A14–A16 are newly added activities or previously unexecuted ones, and it cannot say what produced the difference. [OCC020, OCC021, OCC022]

Other differences: the A40–A41 cycle repeats more often per case, the group around A02/A06/A07/A08 is chosen more often than the group around A01/A03/A04/A05 (about 56/44 versus 47/53 in 100 traces), and small routing shifts occur around A18, A29 and A33–A36; the evidence does not connect these to the restructuring between A39 and A24. [OCC029, OCC030, REL044, OCC001, OCC002, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, DIR002, DIR006, DIR014, DIR025, DIR027]
